LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING - SMS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS, part of Strand 1 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: when writing an SMS, • use SMS observing etiquette. How do we ensure etiquette when using digital devices?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of a Short Message Service (SM

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

S. for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. adopt digital etiquette when using social media for communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. adopt digital etiquette when using social media for communication.

   Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to talk about the features of an ideal SMS,

2. write an SMS using a digital device,

3. peer review another learner’s SMS texts,

4. discuss social media etiquette

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to talk about the features of an ideal SMS,
2. write an SMS using a digital device,
3. peer review another learner’s SMS texts,
4. discuss social media etiquette

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner writes an SMS using a digital device.

• Communication and collaboration: This is improved as the learner discusses and observes social media etiquette when

writing an SMS.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner peer reviews another learner’s SMS texts and gives feedback for

improvement.

• Unity: This is displayed as the learner works jointly with peers to talk about the features of an ideal SMS.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Global citizenship is achieved as the learner is able to apply etiquette in digital communication.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of Short Message Service (SMS) to the concept of modern forms of communication in Social

Studies.
